provenance: Hand-authored repository-search questions grounded in the indexed source snapshot; not production query logs.
relevance_definition: A retrieved chunk is relevant when its source-line interval overlaps the annotated target symbol span.

cases.query: When a Python source file is indexed, where does the parser turn syntax nodes into code chunks?
How does the code indexer avoid splitting a method in the middle, and which syntax units does it keep?
What happens when a small source file has no recognized function or class nodes?
How does the chunking registry choose between Tree-sitter and a fixed-size splitter based on file type?
Where are line-window size and overlap applied when splitting a long text file?
Why can a retrieved code chunk contain a full method while its vector represents only the beginning?
Where is the embedding input cleaned and capped to the model's character limit?
If the local embedding request repeatedly fails, how does the indexing pipeline continue?
How are several code chunks sent to the local embedding service in batches?
Where does the in-memory search combine semantic vector results with BM25 keyword results?
How are BM25 document frequency and average document length prepared when an index loads?
Where does keyword scoring apply term-frequency saturation and document-length normalization?
How does reciprocal-rank fusion merge duplicate results from vector and keyword search?
Where are retrieval candidates compared with expected source files to calculate Recall and MRR?
How does the evaluation code determine the rank of the first expected file?
In the Java implementation, where does Tree-sitter walk source nodes and emit code chunks?
Where does the Java text splitter calculate the next window start from max lines and overlap?
How does the Java retriever obtain vector and keyword candidates for one query?
Where are Java vector and BM25 rankings fused into one ordered list?
Where does the Java Ollama embedder truncate long text before sending the request?
How does the Java indexer rebuild the workspace index from the current source tree?
Before a RAG search, how does the Java tool ensure the active workspace has an index?
Where does the Java RAG tool execute a search and format the matching source context?
Where are access-token claims checked after the signing algorithm has been selected?
Which middleware entry point decides whether a request needs JWT authentication?
How does a protected API handler obtain the verified tenant and subject from request context?
Where does the Python session lane acquire a Redis lock before serializing chat work?
How does the session lane release the lock only when the current worker owns it?
Where is a requested workspace path checked for traversal or escape outside the allowed root?
How does code search invoke ripgrep and turn its matches into bounded results?
Where does the Java file tool normalize a path and reject paths outside its workspace?
How does the Java file tool execute a repository text search and cap the returned matches?
Where does one chat turn hold its session lane while streaming model and tool events?
How does the SQLite checkpoint store claim a recoverable run with a lease?
Where does the tool authorization gate decide whether to invoke a tool or wait for approval?
How does the Python MCP client attach authentication and lineage information to a tool call?
